header: IN THE ISI.AMABAD HIGH COURT, ISLAMABAD,
Asif Fahim Malik through his Special Attorney Muhammad Akif Khan
Respondents by: Sardar Muhammad Ashfaq, Advocate.
body: TARIQ MEHMOOD JAHANGIRI, J: Through the instant criminal appeal filed under Section 4L7 Cr.P.C, the appellant has impugned judgment dated 29.02.2020, passed by tearned Judicial Magistrate Sec.30, West-Islamabad, whereby respondent No. 2 / accused has been acquitted In case F.I.R No. 570/20L5, dated 04.L2.2015, offence UIS 420 P.P.C, registered at P/S Margalla, Islamabad.

02. Brief facts narrated in the instant appeal are that complainant namely Asif Fahim Malik, alleged in instant F.I.R that his late father namely Col. (Retd) Mian Muhammad Khan, who lastly resided in the United States, opened an account No. 173910055206, maintained with UBL Bank, F-8 Markaz, Islamabad. Due to old age and shaky handwriting, father of the complainant authorized brother of the complainant namely Waqar Naeem Malik, to operate said account with his signatures but the same was done under the strict obseruation of his father. The father of the complainant died on 05.02.2015, leaving behind four sons namely Akhtar Saleem Matik, Shahid Atiq Malik, Waqar Naeem Malik (accused) and Asif Fahim Malik, (complainant). That at the time of death, father of the complainant had an amount of Rs. 3,77,30,977.701- in his above mentioned account, which was the rental income of different propefties. After the death of comptainant's father the authority of Waqar Naeem Malik to operate account with his signatures had ceased and the said amount was to be devolved upon al! the legal heirs equally but despite knowing all legal position, the accused, Waqar Naeem Malik came to Pakistan from the U.S.A and by concealing the fact of death of his father from the concerned UBL Bank, he withdrew an amount of Rs. 2,00,000/-, Rs. 3,70,00,000/- and Rs. 5,33,7001- on 11.03.2015, 12.03.2015 and 19.03.2015, respectively from the said account and dishonestly put the said amount to his own use without any legal or moral justification that when the complainant came to know about the misappropriation committed by Waqar Naeem Malik, he came to Pakistan.

03. After conclusion of the investigation, complete repoft / chaltan in the matter within the meaning incorporated in section 173, Cr.P.C was submitted by the prosecution. Copies of statement of allegations were supplied to the accused as required U/S 24t-A, Cr.P.C. Thereafter, charge against the accused was framed on 29.03.20L7 . After recording the evidence and fulfilling al! legal and codal formalities, learned trial Court has acquitted respondent No. 2 / accused vide judgment dated 29.02.2020.

07. It is important to decide the following two objections raised by learned counsel for the respondent No. 2 / accused;
i. Competency of appeal against acquittal, filed through special attorneY.

08. The concept of filing of criminal appeal through attorney is not provided in criminal !aw. There is neither any section of the Criminal Procedure Code (Cr.P.C) nor any other provision of taw on the basis of whlch crimina! appeal can be filed through special attorney. Learned counsel for the appellant has completely failed to point out any law to show that any person can prosecute on behalf of attorney. Reliance in this regard is placed on the following cases:
i.
Quaid Johar Vs. Murtaza Ali and another (PLD 2OO8 Karachi 342)
ii. Ghazanfar Ali Vs. M. Zahid Hussain and others (PLD 2O77 Lahore 779).
iii. Khalid Mehmood and 3 otherc Vs. Safdar fabal and another (2O77 PCnL.J 77O4).

09. As far as second objection with regard to filing of appeal with a delay of L76 days is concerned, for the convenience Section 417(2-A), Cr.P.C is reproduced as under: 4t7, Appeal in case of acguittal:

(2-A) A percon aggrieved by the order of acquittal passed by any Court, other than a High Court, mah within thirty days, file an appeal against such orden 10. The limitation for filing of appeal against acquittal is provided as 30 days in the section supra, as far as the argument of learned counsel for the appellant regarding condonation of delay is concerned, Section 5 of the limitation Act (IX of 1908) for condonation of delay is not applicable to section 417 of the Criminal Procedure Code (Act V of 1898) as clearly laid down under section 29 of the Limitation Act (IX of 1908) which is reproduced as under:

"(7) lllothing in this Act shall affect secttbn 25 of the Contract Act, 7872, (2) Where any special or local law prescribes for any suit, appeat or application a period of limitation different from the period prescribed therefor by the Firct Schedule, the provisions of section 3 shall apply, as if such period were prescribed therefor in that Schedule, and for the purpose of determining any period of timitation prescribed for any suit, appeal or apptication by any special or local law:

(a) the provisions contained in section 4, sections 9 to 7& and section 22 shall apPly only in so far as, and to the extent to which, they are not expressly excluded by such special or local law; and (b) the remaining provisions of this Act shall not aPPlY,"

11. Hence it is clear that if there is a special provision of limitation provided under the relevant law then section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908 will not be applicable for condoning the delay. Retiance is placed upon a case titled as Muhammad Sharif and otherc Vs. The State and otherc eoos MLD 7333).

This Court under the similar fa6 and circumstances of the case reported as Zulfigar Ali v, Superintendent of Police and. otherc (2OO3 SCMR 1562) refused to condone the delay of nearly 5O days while in the present case the delay is of 249 days. Had the appellant visited the copying agency after 27-2-7998 he would have definitety got the ceftified copy as according to him it was prepared on the said date, ft leads to the irresistible conclusion that the appellant never visited copying agency during the period from 27-2-7998 to 7 - 7 O- 7 998."(Emphasis added)

13. The Hon'ble Supreme Couft of Pakistan while dismissing the petition for leave to appeal against acquitta! filed with a delay of one (01) day has held in a case titled as wooI Hussain Vs. Muhammad Salim (7985 SCMR 893), that:

"The petition is, howeve4 barred by time by one day. The petitioner's counsel has not been able to explain the detay satisfadorily. ft appearc that the learned Advocate-on-Record negleded to frle the petition promptty after obtaining the copy of the impugned iudgment, Notwithstanding the fact that the detay is only of one day, we do not consider it a fit case for condonation of the delay as Muhammad satim son of Muhammad Ramzan (respondent No. 7) has acguired the right to live, white otherc have acquired the ualuable right of liberty."

L4. In the case in hand neither any application for the condonation of delay was filed nor any plausible explanation was extended by learned counsel for the appellant, with regard to filing of appea! with an inordinate delay of L76 days. As per dictums laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Pakistan, it is wett settled principle of law that delay of each day has to be satisfactorily explained, ds after expiry of limitation period a vested right is created in favour of the other party which could not be easily brushed aside as the law atways helps the vigilant and not the indolent.
15. It is held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Pakistan in a case titled as Water and Power Development AuthoriU ft988 SCMR 7354) that:

"rt is well settled that after the prescribed period of limitation has elapsed, the door of iustice is closed and no ptea of iniustice, hardship or ignorance can be of any avail unless the detay is propeily explained and accounted fon"

Reliance is atso ptaced upon the cases titled as Khushi MuhammaOl and others Vs. Mst Fazal Bibi and other L2 (pLD 2076 SC 872) and Muhammad sarfraz siyal vs. Fazat Hussain Khan (2O27 CLC 867 -clamabadtt 16. In view of above discussion, I hold that the appea! in criminal case cannot be filed through specia! attorney as well as after an inordinate delay of L76 days, hence instant appeal against acquittal of respondent No. 2 / accused is dismissed being not maintainable.
